title: Guide - Healing and Hope - Hope renewed

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Healing and Hope. <short pause> This practice is called Hope Renewed. <short pause> If hope feels far too large a word today, don't worry. <short pause> We will begin with a very small piece of it.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Settle in, as gently as you can. <short pause> Soften the muscles around your eyes. <short pause> Breathe in, without pulling at the air... <short pause> and breathe out, the way you might near a candle you didn't want to disturb.

After a loss, or a long illness, hope can start to feel dangerous. <short pause> You hoped before, and it hurt. <short pause> So you learn to expect less, and to call that being sensible. <short pause> There is no blame for that here. <short pause> A heart that has been bruised will be careful where it's touched.

Isaiah knew about bruised things. <short pause> He wrote of a servant whom God would send, someone who would not shout, or push, or break down doors. <short pause> And the Gospel of Matthew tells us that this servant is Jesus. <short pause> Here is how gentle He is, in Isaiah forty-two, verse three.
A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench.

A reed was a common, hollow thing. <short pause> If one was bent, you snapped it, and picked another. <short pause> And flax was the wick of a little oil lamp. <short pause> When it burned down to smoke, it was no use for seeing by. <short pause> The sensible thing was to pinch it out.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: But He doesn't snap the reed. <short pause> He doesn't pinch out the wick. <short pause> He bends close to what is nearly finished... <short pause> cups His hands around it... <short pause> and waits with it. <short pause> A bruised reed is safe with Him. <short pause> So are you.

Is there any smoke at all, in you? <short pause> It needn't be a flame. <short pause> A song you still half like. <short pause> A person whose voice you don't mind hearing. <short pause> A faint wish to see the sea again, or a garden in spring. <short pause> Even the wish that you could hope... is a thread of smoke. <short pause> See if you can find one.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Don't blow on it. <short pause> Don't ask it to become a fire. <short pause> Just let His hands be around it, and breathe easily beside it. <short pause> Breathing in... You will not break me. <short pause> Breathing out... You will not put me out. <short pause> Once more. <short pause> You will not break me. <short pause> You will not put me out.

Christian hope is not a promise that everything will go the way we ask. <short pause> It is the promise that Jesus has walked into death itself, and out the other side... <short pause> and that nothing you have lost, and no part of you that is broken, is beyond His reach. <short pause> You don't have to hold that hope perfectly. <short pause> It is strong enough to hold you.

Let's pray. <short pause> Gentle Jesus, here is what is bent in me, and here is what is barely burning. <short pause> Be careful with it, as only You can. <short pause> Guard my small hope from the wind. <short pause> And in Your time, and at Your pace, let there be light in me again. <short pause> Amen.

As you go, watch for one small light. <short pause> A window, a lamp, the screen of a phone with a kind word on it. <short pause> Let it say to you, quietly... <short pause> not quenched. <short pause> Go in hope, however small.
